facts.raw_span: A 3-week-old male Sprague-Dawley rat
appeared clinically normal
euthanized under anesthesia
liver and other organs appeared grossly unremarkable
serum AST and ALT levels were within normal limits
multifocal basophilic foci located predominantly in the perilobular region
polygonal to short spindle-shaped cells formed small nests and sheets within dilated sinusoids without encapsulation
tumor cells exhibited clear cell borders, high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratios, hyperchromatic nuclei, frequent mitotic figures, and sparse hepatocellular necrosis
narrow spaces containing erythrocytes were noted between tumor cells
local invasion into adjacent blood vessels was seen
reticular fibers forming a loosely connected, irregular network within tumor cell aggregates
Azan and silver stains demonstrated
